rationale: B wins because it makes the cleaner strategic call: it refuses the anonymous investor story and treats the utility pilot as a hard-gated trade angle. A keeps "A climate seed fund's bet: the next grid software market is at the community edge" even while admitting the fund is unnamed, then calls it "the only angle that survives the company's thin proof" - no, an anonymous investor thesis does not survive anything. B's "Three utilities are paying to pilot software that shifts demand around local solar output" is risky, but it names the reporting path and says the quiet part properly: "Without a named utility this angle does not exist yet."
gaps_in_A: "the only angle that survives the company's thin proof" overstates the investor angle. With an unnamed lead fund and no partner thesis, there is no protagonist yet.
"ex-Tesla Energy commercial grid experience plus ex-NREL research credibility" decorates the founder facts. The update gives employers, not roles, dates, or evidence of commercial grid work.
A refuses "Three utilities are already paying for community-solar AI" because no utility is named, but keeps the unnamed-fund angle. Same gate, softer treatment.
"community-solar grids as a distinct software market" is plausible, but it is a market claim, not a supplied fact. It needs outside support before a reporter sees it.
gaps_in_B: "someone who shipped commercial energy products at Tesla Energy and someone who did the underlying grid research at a national lab" is invented. The update only says ex-Tesla Energy and ex-NREL.
"Without a named utility this angle does not exist yet" belongs in a parked/refused section, not under a kept customer-story angle, unless the founder can name the utility before pitching.
"local solar output that the wires were not sized for" may be true, but it is more specific than the update. Source it or make it less physical.
"any early measured result, even directional" needs tighter labeling. The update says no independent results, so any metric would have to be clearly described as company-reported or pilot-reported.
